Estimate a regularized Ising network for binary items

Source: R/ising.R
ising_fit.Rd

ising_fit() estimates a regularized Ising network from binary items, such as symptoms that are present or absent or items that are endorsed or not. The Ising model describes the items through a threshold for each item and an interaction for each pair, the association between two items after conditioning on all other items, and is estimated here by the nodewise lasso method of van Borkulo et al. (2014).

A positive edge means that the two items tend to be endorsed together, a negative edge that endorsing one makes the other less likely, and an absent edge that the two are conditionally independent; the network shows which items are directly associated once the rest are taken into account. The function regresses each item on all other items by L1-penalized (lasso) logistic regression and selects each item's penalty by the extended Bayesian information criterion (EBIC). Every pair is estimated twice, once in each item's regression. Under the AND rule (default) an edge is kept when both estimates are nonzero, under the OR rule when either is; its weight is the mean of the two. Rows can be filtered by their sum score (min_sum) and weighted (weights). Each regression is checked against its optimality (Karush–Kuhn–Tucker) conditions, and certificate() reports the largest violation across the items.

The result is an undirected network of class psychnet (psychnet).

For unpenalized estimates with significance-based pruning, use ising_sampler(); for data that combine continuous and binary variables, mgm_fit(). Ordinal or continuous items can be split with dichotomize() first. The model is the one fitted by IsingFit::IsingFit(), which native = FALSE reproduces.

Usage

ising_fit(
  data,
  gamma = 0.25,
  rule = c("AND", "OR"),
  nlambda = 100L,
  lambda_min_ratio = 0.01,
  min_sum = NULL,
  weights = NULL,
  na_method = c("pairwise", "listwise"),
  native = TRUE,
  labels = NULL
)

Arguments

data

Binary data: a data frame or matrix with one row per observation. Columns may be numeric 0/1, logical, or two-level factors (the first level is coded 0). Any other column, such as a numeric column coded 1/2 or a factor with more than two levels, is an error naming it. A constant column is dropped.

gamma

EBIC hyperparameter, a single number >= 0; larger values give sparser networks. Default 0.25.

rule

"AND" (default) keeps an edge when both nodewise estimates are nonzero; "OR" when either is.

nlambda

Number of penalty values on each nodewise path, a whole number >= 2. Default 100.

lambda_min_ratio

Smallest penalty as a fraction of the largest, in (0, 1). Default 0.01. With native = FALSE, leaving it unset uses glmnet's own default, as IsingFit::IsingFit() does.

min_sum

Minimum number of endorsed items per row; rows below it are dropped before fitting. Default NULL keeps every row.

weights

Optional non-negative observation weights, one per row after missing-data handling (and filtered with min_sum). Only their relative sizes matter: weights = w and weights = 7 * w give the same network. Requires native = TRUE. Default NULL (unweighted).

na_method

"pairwise" (default) fills each missing value with the item's more frequent value and keeps every row; "listwise" drops rows with a missing value. The two agree for complete data.

native

TRUE (default) uses the package's own solver. FALSE fits each regression with the glmnet package (which must be installed) and reproduces IsingFit::IsingFit(); its certificate reflects glmnet's convergence tolerance and is usually larger. weights are not accepted with native = FALSE.

labels

Optional node labels: one per node, or one per input column (labels of dropped constant columns are then discarded).

Value

An undirected network of class psychnet (psychnet). as.data.frame() gives one row per edge (from, to, weight), certificate() the largest optimality violation of the nodewise regressions, and net_predict() the predictability of each node. The object also stores the node thresholds (thresholds), the combination rule (rule) and the nodewise regressions (nodewise).

Details

Edge weights and thresholds are on the log-odds scale of the 0/1 coding. The weight of an edge is the change in the log-odds of one item when the other is endorsed, averaged over the two regressions; an item's threshold is its log-odds when every other item is 0.

Conditions

psychnet_bad_input when a column is not binary, fewer than two usable columns remain, gamma, nlambda, lambda_min_ratio, min_sum, weights, native or labels is invalid, min_sum removes every row (or every row with positive weight), weights is combined with native = FALSE, or native = FALSE is requested without the glmnet package; psychnet_constant_variable (warning) when a constant column is dropped; psychnet_no_converge (warning) when a nodewise regression does not reach its optimum; psychnet_degenerate_sample (warning) when an item takes a single value on every retained row, so its regression has no finite intercept. The last two are raised with native = TRUE.

References

van Borkulo, C. D., Borsboom, D., Epskamp, S., Blanken, T. F., Boschloo, L., Schoevers, R. A., & Waldorp, L. J. (2014). A new method for constructing networks from binary data. Scientific Reports, 4, 5918. doi:10.1038/srep05918

Foygel, R., & Drton, M. (2010). Extended Bayesian information criteria for Gaussian graphical models. Advances in Neural Information Processing Systems, 23, 604-612.

See also

ising_sampler() for the unregularized model; mgm_fit() for mixed continuous and binary data; dichotomize() to prepare items; certificate() and glm_lasso_kkt() for the optimality check; net_predict(); psychnet() with method = "ising".

Examples

# Ising models need 0/1 data: split the five SRL construct scores at the median.
b <- dichotomize(SRL_GPT)
fit <- ising_fit(b)
fit
#> <psychnet> ising network
#>   nodes: 5   edges: 6   (undirected)
#>   optimality (KKT residual): 1.45e-09
as.data.frame(fit)
#>   from to    weight
#> 1  CSU IV 2.3063761
#> 2  CSU SE 1.8399656
#> 3   IV SE 1.2860533
#> 4  CSU SR 1.7394177
#> 5   IV SR 1.9836011
#> 6   SE SR 0.7570295
certificate(fit)
#>   method  certificate kind certified
#> 1  ising 1.451526e-09  kkt      TRUE
